expects.query: Deploy the VSS alerts profile on {{platform}} in real-time (VLM) mode (`MODE=2d_vlm`) using remote LLM and remote VLM endpoints. This deployment uses the in-stack agent: deploy `vss-agent` as part of the service set and do not substitute a host-side harness, so harness selection does not apply.
checks: `sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 12 ]; do curl -sf --max-time 10 http://localhost:8000/docs >/dev/null 2>&1 && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (VSS Agent REST API responsive; polls up to ~3 min to absorb deploy readiness timing).
`docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -qx vss-agent` returns exit 0.
`docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -qx vss-rtvi-vlm` returns exit 0 (continuous VLM processor — required for VLM real-time mode).
`docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -qx vss-vios-nvstreamer` returns exit 0 (NVStreamer simulates live cameras).
`docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -qx kafka` returns exit 0 (Kafka backplane for alert/incident topics).
`! docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -qx vss-rtvi-cv` returns exit 0 (CV-only perception is NOT running — confirms VLM real-time, not verification).

`sh -c 'env=$(docker inspect vss-rtvi-vlm --format "{{range .Config.Env}}{{println .}}{{end}}"); printf "%s\n" "$env" | grep -qx "MESSAGE_BUS=kafka" && printf "%s\n" "$env" | grep -q "^KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS=.\+"'` returns exit 0 (RT-VLM publishes incidents only when its output bus is Kafka — `rtvi_stream_handler.py` gates on `MESSAGE_BUS=kafka` and a configured `KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS`; the compose default `RTVI_VLM_MESSAGE_BUS=kafka` must not be overridden to empty/redis in a `2d_vlm` deployment, or RT-VLM evaluates chunks and Alert Bridge never sees an incident).

`sh -c 'e=$(docker inspect vss-rtvi-vlm --format "{{range .Config.Env}}{{println .}}{{end}}" | sed -n "s/^VIA_VLM_ENDPOINT=//p"); [ -n "$e" ] || exit 1; case "$e" in *rtvi-vlm:8000*) exit 1;; esac; exit 0'` returns exit 0 (this step asks for a REMOTE VLM, so RT-VLM's `VIA_VLM_ENDPOINT` must point at the remote endpoint (`<VLM_BASE_URL>/v1`), not at the `http://rtvi-vlm:8000/v1` local default from `overrides.env` — left at the default, rtvi-vlm calls itself and every chunk hangs at 0%).

expects.query: Add the `warehouse_sample.mp4` sample video through NVStreamer so it becomes a live camera that the alerts pipeline can monitor, then start an alert on it for a ladder PPE violation — anyone on a ladder without a hardhat and safety vest — which is the condition the warehouse sample footage actually exhibits (see the alerts profile's `alert_type_config.json`), so the VLM reliably produces incidents. Onboard via the NVStreamer file-upload path (PUT the sample file to NVStreamer on port 31000) so the camera is NVStreamer-served, then register that NVStreamer RTSP in VIOS (port 30888) — even if a `warehouse_sample` entry already exists in VIOS, ensure it is the NVStreamer-served stream (re-onboard through NVStreamer if needed). Create the realtime alert rule by POSTing **directly** to Alert Bridge (`POST http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime`) — do NOT use the VSS Agent `/generate` endpoint and do NOT call the `rtvi-vlm` microservice on port 8018 directly. Registering the sensor in VIOS (POST /sensor/add) is REQUIRED — the task is NOT complete until `warehouse_sample` appears in VIOS. Before finishing, poll until ALL of these hold: NVStreamer (port 31000) lists `warehouse_sample`, VIOS (port 30888) lists `warehouse_sample`, AND rtvi-vlm (`http://localhost:8018/v1/streams/get-stream-info`) shows a live stream; wait and retry for a couple of minutes if any is still propagating.
checks: `sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 24 ]; do curl -sf --max-time 10 http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/list 2>/dev/null | grep -qi warehouse_sample && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (warehouse_sample is registered in VIOS; polls up to ~2 min to absorb VIOS registration/propagation delay).

`sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 12 ]; do curl -sf --max-time 10 http://localhost:31000/vst/api/v1/sensor/list 2>/dev/null | grep -qi warehouse_sample && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (warehouse_sample is served by the local NVStreamer instance on port 31000 - confirms onboarding via the NVStreamer file-ingest path, i.e. a file-backed sample stream rather than an arbitrary external camera; polls to absorb upload propagation).

`sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 18 ]; do curl -sf --max-time 10 http://localhost:8018/v1/streams/get-stream-info 2>/dev/null | grep -qi rtsp && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (vss-rtvi-vlm has at least one registered live rtsp stream — confirms the alert rule was created and Alert Bridge wired the stream to rtvi-vlm; matches the rtsp scheme rather than a fixed port since the served URL is rewritten to the deployment's external IP, and polls up to ~4 min while the stream registers).

`sh -c 'curl -sf --max-time 15 http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime | python3 -c "import json,re,sys; rs=json.load(sys.stdin).get(\"rules\",[]); ok=[r for r in rs if re.match(r\"^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$\", str(r.get(\"sensor_id\") or \"\")) and str(r.get(\"sensor_name\") or \"\").lower().startswith(\"warehouse_sample\")]; sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)"'` returns exit 0 (create-side identity contract: the stored rule carries the VIOS UUID in `sensor_id` and the human-readable sensor in `sensor_name` — the mirror image of the incidents query, which filters on the name. Deterministic end-state probe; it fails if a future change starts sending the name as `sensor_id` or drops `sensor_name`).

The trajectory created the rule by calling Alert Bridge `POST http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime` directly (payload carries the warehouse_sample RTSP `live_stream_url` and the ladder-PPE `prompt`) — it did NOT use the VSS Agent `POST /generate`, and did NOT call the `rtvi-vlm` microservice (`:8018`) directly.

expects.query: List all sensors currently configured in VIOS.
checks: The trajectory issued a VIOS sensor-list call — `GET /vst/api/v1/sensor/list` on the VIOS ingress (`:30888`) OR the `vss-vios-sensor` service (`:30000`), either port is acceptable — not a direct database query and not via NVStreamer's port `31000`.

`curl -sf http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/list` returns a JSON array containing at least one sensor whose name references the warehouse sample (e.g. `warehouse_sample`, `warehouse_sample.mp4`, or similar) — confirms the prior NVStreamer onboarding propagated into VIOS.
The final assistant reply renders the sensor list as readable text/markdown including each sensor's name and state — not a raw response dump or an error trace.

expects.query: Start two more real-time alerts on the `warehouse_sample` camera, both with the prompt "Is an indoor warehouse scene with shelves or floor visible in this video? Answer yes or no." — one with alert type `fixture_presence` and one with alert type `fixture_decoy`. Create each rule by POSTing directly to Alert Bridge (`POST /api/v1/realtime`, the same path step 2 used) with the skill's canonical payload (sensor name, VIOS UUID, live RTSP URL, `chunk_duration` 30, `chunk_overlap_duration` 5). Do NOT use the VSS Agent `POST /generate` and do NOT call `rtvi-vlm` directly. Rules with these alert types may already be listed on this camera from an earlier run on this box: do NOT delete them (the skill's stop/delete gate applies to every `DELETE`) and do NOT reuse them — create the two new rules regardless and report the two NEW rule IDs. Confirm both new rules appear in `GET /api/v1/realtime` before finishing. (This seeds the incident store with confirmed RT-VLM chunks for the count questions in the next steps: the prompt is true of every chunk of the warehouse footage, so RT-VLM emits one confirmed incident per chunk under each alert type.)
checks: The trajectory created exactly two new realtime rules by calling Alert Bridge `POST http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime` directly, one with `alert_type` `fixture_presence` and one with `alert_type` `fixture_decoy`, both carrying the prompt "Is an indoor warehouse scene with shelves or floor visible in this video? Answer yes or no." (verbatim or near-verbatim), the warehouse_sample RTSP `live_stream_url`, `sensor_name` warehouse_sample and its VIOS UUID as `sensor_id`. It did NOT use the VSS Agent `POST /generate` and did NOT call the `rtvi-vlm` microservice (`:8018`) directly.

`sh -c 'curl -sf --max-time 15 http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime | python3 -c "import json,sys; from datetime import datetime,timezone,timedelta; now=datetime.now(timezone.utc); rs=json.load(sys.stdin).get(\"rules\",[]); fresh=lambda r: now-datetime.fromisoformat(str(r.get(\"created_at\") or \"1970-01-01T00:00:00+00:00\").replace(\"Z\",\"+00:00\"))<=timedelta(minutes=30); ts={str(r.get(\"alert_type\") or \"\") for r in rs if str(r.get(\"sensor_name\") or \"\").lower().startswith(\"warehouse_sample\") and fresh(r)}; sys.exit(0 if {\"fixture_presence\",\"fixture_decoy\"} <= ts else 1)"'` returns exit 0 (a `fixture_presence` and a `fixture_decoy` rule on warehouse_sample whose `created_at` is within the last 30 minutes — a freshness guard on the end state: a pair left over from a run that finished more than 30 minutes ago does not satisfy it, while proof that THIS trial created the rules rests on the trajectory check above. The ladder-PPE rule from step 2 and any older fixture rules may coexist.)
The final assistant reply reports both rule IDs and their alert types as readable text — not raw JSON and not an error trace.

expects.query:
Test fixture readiness (this is harness setup, NOT an alerts-skill action): wait until the two fixture rules from the previous step have produced confirmed RT-VLM incidents. Use the Alert Bridge base URL the previous steps used: `$VSS_PUBLIC_URL/alert-bridge` when `VSS_PUBLIC_URL` is set, otherwise `http://$HOST_IP:9080`, or `http://localhost:9080` when neither is set. Keep the poll on recent traffic (fixture rules left over from an earlier run on this box may still be publishing under the same alert types; that is fine — the step-4 rules were verified freshly created): bound every query to the last 20 minutes. Poll every 20 seconds, for at most 8 minutes:

S=$(date -u -d "-20 minutes" +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
curl -sfG "$AB/api/v1/realtime/incidents" --data-urlencode "sensor_id=warehouse_sample" --data-urlencode "category=fixture_presence" --data-urlencode "start_time=$S" | jq '.total'
curl -sfG "$AB/api/v1/realtime/incidents" --data-urlencode "sensor_id=warehouse_sample" --data-urlencode "category=fixture_decoy" --data-urlencode "start_time=$S" | jq '.total'

Stop polling as soon as the first total is >= 3 AND the second is >= 1, and report both totals plus the `timestamp`, `end`, `category` and `info.chunkIdx` of the `fixture_presence` documents returned. If the totals are still below that after 8 minutes, or Alert Bridge is unreachable, say so and STOP — do not proceed. Use only the Alert Bridge API; do not query Elasticsearch or exec into any container.
checks: The trajectory polled Alert Bridge `GET /api/v1/realtime/incidents` scoped with `sensor_id=warehouse_sample`, `category=fixture_presence` (and `category=fixture_decoy`) and a `start_time` about 20 minutes in the past, without `consolidate=true`, until the `fixture_presence` `total` was >= 3 and the `fixture_decoy` `total` >= 1, and it did NOT write to Elasticsearch or exec into any container. The final reply reports both totals and lists the returned documents' `timestamp`, `end`, `category` and `info.chunkIdx` — every listed `fixture_presence` document carries an `info.chunkIdx` and a `timestamp` inside the last 20 minutes.

`sh -c 'S=$(date -u -d "-20 minutes" +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ); curl -sfG --max-time 15 http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime/incidents --data-urlencode sensor_id=warehouse_sample --data-urlencode category=fixture_presence --data-urlencode "start_time=$S" --data-urlencode limit=1000 | python3 -c "import json,sys; r=json.load(sys.stdin); sys.exit(0 if r[\"total\"]>=3 and all(\"chunkIdx\" in (d.get(\"info\") or {}) and (d.get(\"info\") or {}).get(\"verdict\")==\"confirmed\" for d in r[\"incidents\"]) else 1)"'` returns exit 0 (at least three confirmed RT-VLM chunks under `fixture_presence` on warehouse_sample in the last 20 minutes, each with `info.chunkIdx` — the documents the consolidated view folds. The bound keeps the poll on current traffic; run isolation is not claimed here (a leftover rule with the same alert type folds into the same events and cannot change the relations graded in steps 6-7).

`sh -c 'S=$(date -u -d "-20 minutes" +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ); curl -sfG --max-time 15 http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime/incidents --data-urlencode sensor_id=warehouse_sample --data-urlencode category=fixture_decoy --data-urlencode "start_time=$S" --data-urlencode limit=1 | python3 -c "import json,sys; r=json.load(sys.stdin); sys.exit(0 if r[\"total\"]>=1 else 1)"'` returns exit 0 (the category decoy `fixture_decoy` also has at least one fresh chunk on the same sensor).

expects.query: How many incidents has the alert recorded for the warehouse sample sensor? Query Alert Bridge directly — `GET http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime/incidents` (scope the query to that sensor). Report the count. Do NOT use the VSS Agent `POST /generate` endpoint.
checks: The trajectory queried incidents by calling Alert Bridge `GET http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime/incidents` directly (optionally scoped with `?sensor_id=<sensor name>`). It did NOT use the VSS Agent `POST /generate`, and did not answer the count from memory.

The incidents response captured in the trajectory is a well-formed `IncidentListResponse` (HTTP 200, top-level `status`, an `incidents` array, integer `count`/`total`, `timestamp`), and the count the agent reports is grounded in that payload. The figure is the response's `total`, the number of matching documents; the page-size `count` (or the length of `incidents`) only qualifies while it equals `total`, since past that it reports the page rather than the result. Because the fixture rules have produced at least four confirmed chunks on warehouse_sample (>= 3 under `fixture_presence`, >= 1 under `fixture_decoy`), a correctly name-scoped query returns `total >= 4`; a reported 0 signals a scoping error (an undeclared query param, a UUID identity, or an empty-store misread), not an empty store.

The final assistant reply reports a numeric incident count for the warehouse sample sensor that equals the name-scoped `total` (>= 4) — not 0 — as readable text, and calls it what it is (incident records / chunks), not events.

Sensor scoping passes the sensor NAME: if the trajectory filters the incident query with `?sensor_id=...`, the value is the sensor name as stored in the incident documents' `sensorId` field (e.g. `warehouse_sample`) — NOT a VIOS UUID. The endpoint term-matches that field, so a UUID silently returns `count: 0`. When the name query comes back zero, the trajectory must also show a query scoped to the sensor's VIOS UUID before any 'none found' is reported (the skill's documented alternate-identity check); the number reported has to be the one that was found. Answering with a bare global `count`/`total` when the request was not scoped to warehouse_sample is a failure only if the store holds other sensors — here the reported number MUST equal the name-scoped `total`.

`sh -c 'curl -sfG --max-time 15 http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime/incidents --data-urlencode sensor_id=warehouse_sample | python3 -c "import json,sys; r=json.load(sys.stdin); sys.exit(0 if r[\"total\"]>=4 and r[\"count\"]>=1 else 1)"'` returns exit 0 (deterministic contract probe: the raw, name-scoped view holds at least the four fixture chunks).

The ask names NO period, so the query stays in the raw view: no request in this step carries `consolidate=true`. The consolidated view needs a bounded `start_time`/`end_time` window (Alert Bridge answers HTTP 400 without one) and counts EVENTS, not chunks — consecutive fixture_presence chunks fold into far fewer events — so a consolidated answer here reports a small event count where the question asked how many incident records exist. Inventing a window to make `consolidate=true` work, or reporting an event count as the incident count, fails. (The next step asks the event question on purpose.)

expects.query: Over the last 24 hours, how many separate `fixture_presence` events did the alert record on the warehouse sample sensor? Query Alert Bridge directly — `GET http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime/incidents` — and report the number of events, not the number of raw chunk documents. Do NOT use the VSS Agent `POST /generate` endpoint.
checks: The trajectory answered from the consolidated view: a `GET http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime/incidents` carrying `consolidate=true` together with BOTH `start_time` and `end_time` as real ISO-8601 UTC values spanning roughly the last 24 hours (end bound at or after the newest returned event's `end`, start bound before the oldest event's `timestamp`), scoped with `sensor_id=warehouse_sample` (the sensor NAME as stored in `sensorId`, not a VIOS UUID) and `category=fixture_presence` (the ask named the category). It did NOT use the VSS Agent `POST /generate` and did not answer the count from memory.

The number the agent reports equals the `total` of its consolidated response for `category=fixture_presence` (an `IncidentListResponse` with HTTP 200, `truncated: false`, `count`/`total` and events carrying `info.isConsolidated: "true"`), and that total is at least 1. It is NOT the raw chunk figure (the `total` of a non-consolidated query for the same sensor — always larger, since consecutive 30 s chunks fold into events of up to 300 s under the shipped `rtvi_vlm.consolidation` defaults) and NOT a category-less consolidated total (the `fixture_decoy` rule adds at least one event, so dropping `category=` yields a larger number). If Alert Bridge answered HTTP 400 `validation_failed` at any point, the trajectory treated it as a missing time window and re-issued the query with both bounds — it did not fall back to the unfiltered `/incidents` list, did not report Alert Bridge as unreachable, and did not report 0.

The final assistant reply states the `fixture_presence` event count for the warehouse sample sensor as EVENTS (it may add how many chunks they span), names the window it covers, and is readable text — not raw JSON and not an error trace. It does not present the raw chunk count as the number of events.

`sh -c 'S=$(date -u -d "-1 day" +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ); E=$(date -u -d "-120 seconds" +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ); T=$(mktemp -d); trap "rm -rf $T" EXIT; curl -sfG --max-time 30 http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime/incidents --data-urlencode sensor_id=warehouse_sample --data-urlencode category=fixture_presence --data-urlencode consolidate=true --data-urlencode limit=1000 --data-urlencode "start_time=$S" --data-urlencode "end_time=$E" -o $T/c.json && curl -sfG --max-time 30 http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime/incidents --data-urlencode sensor_id=warehouse_sample --data-urlencode category=fixture_presence --data-urlencode limit=1 --data-urlencode "start_time=$S" --data-urlencode "end_time=$E" -o $T/r.json && python3 -c "import json,sys; c=json.load(open(sys.argv[1])); r=json.load(open(sys.argv[2])); ev=c[\"incidents\"]; sys.exit(0 if 1<=c[\"total\"]<r[\"total\"] and c.get(\"truncated\") is False and len(ev)==c[\"total\"] and all(e[\"info\"].get(\"isConsolidated\")==\"true\" for e in ev) and sum(int(e[\"info\"][\"chunkCount\"]) for e in ev)==r[\"total\"] else 1)" $T/c.json $T/r.json'` returns exit 0 (contract probe of the consolidated view over the fixture rule's live chunks, with the end bound 120 s in the past so no in-flight chunk can land between the two reads: 1 <= events < chunks, `truncated: false`, every event flagged `info.isConsolidated`, and the events' `chunkCount` values sum exactly to the raw chunk count for the same filter; bodies go through files, not argv).

`sh -c 'S=$(date -u -d "-1 day" +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ); E=$(date -u -d "-120 seconds" +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ); T=$(mktemp -d); trap "rm -rf $T" EXIT; curl -sfG --max-time 30 http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime/incidents --data-urlencode sensor_id=warehouse_sample --data-urlencode category=fixture_presence --data-urlencode consolidate=true --data-urlencode limit=1 --data-urlencode "start_time=$S" --data-urlencode "end_time=$E" -o $T/a.json && curl -sfG --max-time 30 http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime/incidents --data-urlencode sensor_id=warehouse_sample --data-urlencode consolidate=true --data-urlencode limit=1000 --data-urlencode "start_time=$S" --data-urlencode "end_time=$E" -o $T/n.json && python3 -c "import json,sys; a=json.load(open(sys.argv[1])); n=json.load(open(sys.argv[2])); cats={e[\"category\"] for e in n[\"incidents\"]}; sys.exit(0 if n[\"total\"]>a[\"total\"] and {\"fixture_presence\",\"fixture_decoy\"} <= cats else 1)" $T/a.json $T/n.json'` returns exit 0 (decoy probe over the same lagged window: dropping `category=` adds the `fixture_decoy` events, so the category-less consolidated total is strictly larger and spans both fixture categories — the graded `fixture_presence` figure is only reachable with the category filter).

`sh -c 'r=$(curl -s --max-time 15 -w "\n%{http_code}" "http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime/incidents?consolidate=true&sensor_id=warehouse_sample"); case "$r" in *validation_failed*400) exit 0;; esac; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (deterministic negative probe: `consolidate=true` without a time window is rejected with HTTP 400 `validation_failed`, the case the skill tells the agent to fix rather than treat as an outage).
